text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank enters the currency board system today with 2.7 billion marks in foreign exchange reserves to cover BNB liabilities of 2.2 trillion levs, a senior official said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim said four gasoline tanks exploded near the refinery's gasoline terminal, but declined to elaborate on the possible cause of the explosion, in which nobody was hurt.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet urged state owned firms to file suits against their debtors in a move to boost budget revenue and tighten financial discipline under the currency board system, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said. Companies owed some 190 billion levs in unpaid bills to the state energy firms by the end of March.
-- Neftochim said it may raise retail surcharges to its biggest clients to 35 percent from 25 percent.
-- Bulgaria's gross foreign debt fell by $165 million in the first quarter of this year to $9.494 billion, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's lottery Toto-2 said the jackpot for this week has reached an all time high of 150 million levs.
-- Bulgaria's Health Ministry said it had registered 21 HIV positive Bulgarians this year, bringing the total registered in the country to 208.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet postponed an expected increase of electricity and central heating charges until mid-August, Trade Minister Valentin Vassilev said.

-- The mayor of Bulgaria's southeast Black Sea town of Primorsko Dimitar Dimitrov said he had banned playing of music in local pubs after 1 a.m. to tighten control on public order. The mayor's office said it would cut electricity supply to pub managers who neglect the order.
-- Bulgaria's government raised licence fees on military production exports to six million levs annually from 300,000 levs, the cabinet press centre said.

-- Bulgaria may sell canned vegetables, clothes and shoes worth some $3 million annually to Jordan's army under a bilateral agreement expected to be sealed in the next few months, the Bulgarian-Arab Trade and Industry Chamber said.
-- Bulgaria has started to rotate customs officers at border checkpoints in a move to fight corruption, a customs official said.
